description: A production-oriented HTTP API built around the existing PHP Bale client, with persistent database storage.

services.name: Bale HTTP API
services.description: Expose selected Bale client capabilities through a secure, documented HTTP API and persist required application data.

answers.baleApiScope: All operations supported by the existing PHP client

questions.question: Which language should power the HTTP API? Keeping PHP makes it easiest to reuse the existing Bale client.

options.label: PHP
options.description: Reuse the existing PHP Bale client directly; recommended.

options.label: TypeScript (Node.js)
options.description: Build a TypeScript API and integrate or port the Bale client as needed.

options.label: Python
options.description: Build a Python API and integrate or port the Bale client as needed.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Build a .NET API and integrate or port the Bale client as needed.

questions.rationale: The provided source project is a PHP Bale client, so PHP minimizes rewrite risk.

questions.question: Which framework/runtime should host the API? You can choose Azure Functions or enter a custom framework (for example Laravel or Symfony).

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: Use a serverless HTTP API; PHP requires a compatible custom-handler/runtime approach.

questions.rationale: A conventional PHP framework such as Laravel is a strong fit for a persistent, versioned HTTP API; confirm the framework choice.

questions.question: Which persistent stores should the API use? Select every store needed; the database is required. Add Blob Storage if the API should retain or serve uploaded/media files.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational database for API records, configuration, and durable application state.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Managed SQL Server database for relational application data.

options.label: MySQL
options.description: Relational database option compatible with common PHP stacks.

options.label: Redis
options.description: Optional cache, rate-limit, or queue coordination store.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Durable storage for files or media retained or served by the API.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Only for a stateless API; do not combine with another store.

questions.rationale: PostgreSQL is a robust default for the requested persistent database; confirm the engine and whether files/media need durable storage.

questions.question: Should callers sign in to use the API's application features? This is about API users, not Azure credentials or which identity provider to use.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require authenticated callers for protected API operations.

options.label: No
options.description: Expose the API without user sign-in; sensitive operations still need an explicit protection strategy.

questions.rationale: A public API that can act on Bale accounts should generally authenticate callers.

questions.question: Which Bale client operations should become HTTP endpoints? List must-have operations and any exclusions. Consider messages, chats/groups, contacts, media/file transfer, webhooks, and account/session management; scope only capabilities supported by the source client.
questions.rationale: The API surface and security boundaries depend on which existing client capabilities you want exposed.

questions.question: Where should the first production deployment run? You can refine availability and scaling requirements in the response.

options.label: Azure App Service
options.description: Managed hosting for a conventional web API; a natural fit for a PHP framework.

options.label: Azure Container Apps
options.description: Container-based hosting with flexible scaling and background-work options.

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: Serverless hosting, subject to language/runtime and execution-model fit.

options.label: Other / decide later
options.description: Specify another cloud, self-hosted environment, or defer the choice.

questions.rationale: Azure App Service is a straightforward managed deployment option for a PHP HTTP API.
